texts.preamble: Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Kabc080005592020 Presented on : 14-01-2020 Registered on : 14-01-2020 Decided on : 23-01-2024 Duration : 4 years, 0 months, 9 days : 3 years, 11 months, 6 days In The Court Of The Metropolitan Magistrate, Traffic Court - Vi, At Bengaluru Dated This 23 Rd Day Of January 2024. Present : Smt.AKHILA H.K. B.A., Ll.B., M.M.T.C-Vi, Bengaluru. Crl.Misc.No.129/2019
texts.facts: The present petition is filed by the petitioners under Sec.12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. 2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under; The petitioner is the legally wedded wife of respondent and their marriage was solemnized on 27.08.2010. They have a girl child by name Poorvi N born on 14.04.2014. After the marriage the petitioner and respondent started to live at matrimonial house situated at Kempegowdanagara, Gooleharavi with her in laws and they led happy marital life only for few months after that respondent and his family members ill treated the petitioner and started to demand dowry from her parents. Further respondent made the petitioner to go to her parents house situated at Bangalore thereafter also the 3 Crl.Misc.129/2019 respondent personally as well as telepathically tortured her and her parents and demanded dowry for a sum of Rs.20 lakhs. When she and her parents were unable to fulfill the demands of the respondent and his family members they started to ill treat by abusing, assaulting and torturing physically and causing mental agony to the petitioner. Further respondent and his family members threatened to do away with the life of the petitioner and her family members. The respondent has not provided food and clothing and shelter for her livelihood. Petitioner further submits that she tolerated the atrocities of the respondent under the impression that one or the other day respondent will improve and realize his mistakes and will take the petitioner to the matrimonial home and they may live happily. Further she submits that, respondent never came to look after the pregnant woman before giving birth to a child and further not even a single day the respondent or his parents came to see the child as well as the petitioner. Further she submits that, respondent is an employee in Government Department as a First Division Clerk in BEO Office at Tumkur and he getting a monthly salary of Rs.65,000/- and he is getting monthly income around one lakh from agriculture property and other sources. In spite of having sufficient source of income he neglected to maintain her and her child. Hence, this petition. 3. After the service of notice, respondent appeared before this court through his counsel and filed statement of objection and in the statement of objection he has admitted his relationship with the petitioner and admitted that they have daughter from the wedlock and he denied all the other allegations. He has stated that, he and his family members never demanded dowry and they never caused domestic violence against the petitioner. 3 examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 4. The respondent has led his evidence and got marked Ex.R.1 to 11. 6 Crl.Misc.129/2019 5.
texts.arguments: Further she submits that, she went to the respondent's house many times and petitioner was pushed out of the matrimonial house without any valid reasons. Further she submits that, respondent and his family members picked up a quarrel near the house of the petitioner and forcibly sent the petitioner to her father house. Further 4 Crl.Misc.129/2019 Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102766219/ 2 she submits that, she is not having any avocation of her own and she is a home maker and her father's income is very low and they are unable to take care of the petitioner. Further he submits that, he admitted his daughter to school and he has borne the entire educational expenses of the child. Further he submits that, he is residing at Tumkur as he is working at BEO Office, Tumkur and he owns ancestral property near Tumkur and he is not 5 Crl.Misc.129/2019 intending to reside at Bengaluru but the petitioner forced him to reside in Bengaluru and to arrange a house at Bengaluru and when he denied petitioner's demand she voluntarily deserted him and went to her parents house. Further after a panchayath was convened for reunion, he rented a house at Tumkur and admitted his daughter to a school at Tumkur but there also petitioner and her parents picked up a quarrel with him and again petitioner went to her parents house. Further he submits that, petitioner restricted her daughter to talk with him. Further he submits that he is not receiving salary of Rs.65,000/-. Further he submits that, after deducting loan he is receiving salary of Rs.26,000/- per month. Further he submits that, till now he is paying the rent of the Tumkur house which was arranged by him for the petitioner. Further he submits that, he has not deserted the petitioner, the petitioner has voluntarily deserted him and started to reside at her parents house. On all these grounds he prays to dismiss the petition filed by the petitioner. 4. The petitioner to substantiate her case has Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102766219/ Hence, she was forced to leave to her parents house. She has alleged that, the respondent never looked after her even when she was pregnant and he and his parents never came to see the child or her. She has stated that, she has taken a rented house for herself and she requires money for advance and to pay the rent of the house. In this regard she has produced rent agreement dated 05.07.2019 which discloses that she has paid Rs.80,000/- as advance and Rs.8,000/- per monthly rent to the house owner. She has stated that, her parents have arranged for the said amount . She has further stated that, she requires Rs.12,000/- for domestic expenses and her child's expenses, Rs.10,000/- for other expenses and monthly maintenance of Rs.20,000/-. She has stated that since the respondent is a government employee and getting monthly income of Rs.;65,000/- he is capable of maintaining her. 11. The respondent in this case has contended that the petitioner was not willing to residing with him in Tumkur and she wished to reside in Bengaluru. Hence, she has voluntarily left the matrimonial home. She has stated that, the respondent rented at house at Tumkur after a panchayath was conducted between them. She has denied all the other suggestions put forth to her and stated that, she resided in a separate house only after it was resolved in the panchayath that herself and respondent should stay in the separate house. She has admitted that she has not given any complaint to the police against the respondent and she does not have any documents to show that the respondent has assaulted her. She has stated that she has left the matrimonial home in July 2019. 12. The respondent has admitted that he has filed for divorce against the petitioner in MC 256/2019 and he has produced the copy of the order sheet as Ex.R.1. He has stated that, the petitioner did not appear before the Hon'ble Family Court and she was placed ex-parte. Thereafter the said Hon'ble Court granted him divorce by its judgment dated 17.01.2020. This conduct of the respondent proves that he was least interested in continuing his marital life with the petitioner. The conduct of the respondent itself constitutes domestic violence. 13. The respondent has contended that, he has paid for the school fees and other expenses of the child. However he has not produced any documents to prove his contention. He has submitted that the Hon'ble Family Court in MC 256/2019 by its order dated 21.10.2022 has ordered for interim maintenance of Rs.6,000/- per month to the petitioner from the date of the application till disposal of the petition and has also ordered litigation expenses of Rs.5,000/- to the petitioner. In Cross Examination respondent has submitted that, he is paying the said interim Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102766219/ 7 maintenance regularly. But before the said order for interim maintenance the respondent has not paid any amount to the petitioner or her child. This also proves the economic abuse caused by the respondent. Further the respondent has contended that, petitioners siblings are all government employees and earning Rs.65,000/- 13 Crl.Misc.129/2019 per month. Even her father is a retired government employee and has many immovable properties in Tumkur and Bengaluru. Therefore, the petitioner does not required any maintenance. But it is settled law by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Manish Jain V/s Akanksha Jain reported in AIR 2017 Supreme Court 1640, that the income of the parents should not be considered while deciding the maintenance of the parties. Hence, the salary of the siblings of the petitioner and properties of the father of the petitioner is immaterial for the present case. The petitioner in this case has sought for Rs.20,000/- monthly maintenance. Admittedly, the petitioner is unemployed. She has stated that, she requires Rs.40,000/- for her monthly maintenance. Petitioner has stated that she requires Rs.1.5 lakhs towards child maintenance and education. Petitioner has stated that she is residing with her parents. She has stated that she is incurring litigation expenses of Rs.5,000/-. The Hon'ble Family Court in MC No.256/2019 has ordered interim maintenance of Rs.6,000/- per month to the petitioner and litigation expenses of Rs.5,000/-. 16. On the other hand the respondent is working Chitra D 8660454326 vs Nandish Kumar on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102766219/ 8 as a Superintendent in BEO office, Nelamangala and he is earning Rs.52,881/- per month as per his assets and liabilities affidavit. He has stated that, he has monthly expenditure of Rs.54,128/-. He has stated that, he has remarried and he has his 2nd wife, 9 months old baby from the said marriage. He has stated that, his aged mother and his 2nd wife and child are his dependents. He has stated that he has paid Rs.30,000/- per annum towards education of the petitioner's child. However, he has not substantiated this expenditure with documents. The petitioner has not admitted regarding this payment made by the respondent. Therefore, the respondent has to prove that he has paid Rs.30,000/- per annum towards his child education. As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajanesh V/s Neha reported in (2021) 2 SCC 324, the Court has to consider the status of the parties, earning capacity of the parties, needs and expenses of the petitioner, number of dependents on the respondent, expenses of the respondent, educational qualification of the parties, whether the petitioner has independent source and whether the same is sufficient to enable her to maintain herself, standard of living as she was accustomed to in the matrimonial home, whether she was working before 16 Crl.Misc.129/2019 marriage, cost of litigation for a non working wife etc., while ordering for maintenance.
